newsitem.title: USA: Teleglobe pushes into U.S. phone market.
newsitem.headline: Teleglobe pushes into U.S. phone market.

text.p: Canadian firm Teleglobe Inc on Wednesday announced a two-pronged offensive into the international telephone market for U.S. based customers.

In one move, Teleglobe said it would offer low-cost international communications to large businesses across 10 U.S. cities by the second quarter. Service was offered as of Wednesday in New York, where Teleglobe is opening an office.
Secondly, Teleglobe said it tied up a deal allowing users of Ameritech Corp's calling card to call home or any one of 240 countries when they are abroad. Users can also make collect calls.
The 10-city rollout of low-cost calling was the first foray into directly offering business market calling for Teleglobe, which has been mainly a carrier of traffic for other telecom companies.

Details of the deals were revealed by Reuters on Tuesday, when sources close to the deals said Ameritech and two other regional Bells, BellSouth Corp and Bell Atlantic Corp had signed contracts to use Teleglobe.
The sources said that although the first deals will be calling card deals, a broader use of Teleglobe's satellite and undersea cables by the Bells is expected.

The regional Bells need to get international calling capabilities as well as access to domestic long distance calling to be ready to fight for long distance customers when they are allowed into that market, analysts say.

The 1996 Telecom Act said Bells can only offer long distance calling -- domestic or international -- when their own local calling markets are open to competition, a condition that industry executives expect to satisfy during this year.
The services will be provided through Teleglobe International, Teleglobe's global carrier subsidiary. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
